feasibility.rationale: This property is fundamentally incompatible with group-house living for multiple blocking reasons: (1) FOR SALE at $25M—group leasing requires an investor/owner willing to lease back, which is virtually unheard of at this price tier; trophy properties sell to owner-occupants or investors seeking appreciation, not rental yield. (2) The 2026 Decorator Showcase renovation positions this as a museum-quality showpiece—no landlord would expose $25M of bespoke finishes, hand-painted murals, and custom marble to group-house wear. (3) Prestige mismatch: this is a landmark mansion designed for a single wealthy family or executive, not a coliving arrangement. The architectural integrity, original millwork, and 9 fireplaces are assets for a private estate, liabilities for group durability. (4) Even if an investor agreed to lease it, $70k/mo rent (~$280k annual vs $25M purchase = 1.1% yield) makes zero financial sense; they'd want $15-20k/mo minimum for viable returns, making per-person cost astronomical. Verdict: this is a once-in-a-generation sale of a San Francisco landmark. A group of friends cannot move in soon—or likely ever.

This is a FOR SALE property at $6.975M, not a rental. Acquisition or master-lease negotiation at this price point is extremely challenging for a group house. The description mentions 67 Belcher is currently leased month-to-month and 69 Belcher (the warehouse studio) 'can be delivered vacant,' suggesting some flexibility, but no indication the owner is interested in a long-term group lease vs. selling to a developer (property is approved for 31-unit condo conversion). The property is spectacular and move-in ready with incredible amenities, but accessing it requires either purchasing at $7M or convincing the owner to do a creative lease arrangement instead of selling—both are long shots for a group-house search.

feasibility.rationale: MAJOR RED FLAG: Description explicitly states 3 of 4 units are tenant-occupied with in-place income, only the oversized 3BR unit is vacant. For a group-house lease, you need the entire building vacant. SF tenant protections make evicting existing tenants extremely difficult—requires just cause (Ellis Act, owner move-in, etc.), 120+ days notice, relocation payments averaging $7k-$20k per tenant, and potential legal challenges. Even if buyer negotiates vacant possession at close, existing tenants have strong legal protections and the process typically takes 6-12+ months. The one vacant 3BR unit could theoretically house 3-4 people immediately, but that defeats the purpose of an 8-person group house. Unless the seller pre-negotiates buyouts with all tenants or uses Ellis Act (which requires taking the entire building off rental market for 5+ years), this is not realistically move-in ready for a whole-building group lease. Best case: 6-12 month timeline with significant legal/buyout costs. Worst case: tied up in litigation for years.
